text:
maria: Heads up — NVD posted CVE-2026-21234 (jackson-databind polymorphic deserialization RCE). Exploits observed in the wild. https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-21234
liam: ack. any initial CVSS or vendor advisory?
maria: CVSS 9.1 in the advisory. Vendor says 2.15.4+ contains the fix.
cheng: tagging infra teams. Which services use jackson directly vs shaded via libs?
anita: running quick repo scan now: `rg "com\.fasterxml\.jackson" --hidden --glob '!vendor/**'`
devops-bot: automated-scan: 7 repos flagged with jackson-databind < 2.15.4 (services: inference-worker, model-ingest, telemetry-ingest)
liam: OK prioritize inference-worker and model-ingest. Those process untrusted payloads.
maria: agree. attack surface high for model-ingest since it deserializes user-provided model metadata.
derek: I'm on inference-worker. I'll open PRs to upgrade and run integration tests. Assign to ENG-712.
anita: i'll take model-ingest and telemetry-ingest follow-up. ENG-713.
liam: quick mitigation while patches roll out: add a strict content-type + JSON schema validation gate to endpoints that accept model metadata. Also add WAF rule to block suspicious __type fields.
cheng: can we push a temporary feature flag reject on polymorphic markers? we already have a middleware for disallowed fields.
anita: yep middleware toggle in api-gateway. I can flip for model-ingest.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for model-ingest v2.4.1-canary at 1799996400
maria: communication: security bulletin to customers? It's exploited in the wild but we haven't seen indicators against our infra yet. Recommend internal comms first.
liam: internal PSAs to infra, dev, and support teams. Customer comms only if we detect exploitation or if customers ask.
derek: upgrade notes: jackson 2.15.4 requires minor API changes for our custom deserializers. I'll push a compatibility branch and PR: https://git.internal/redwood/inference-worker/pull/1123
anita: model-ingest PR: https://git.internal/redwood/model-ingest/pull/987 — includes schema validation and jackson bumped to 2.15.4. Tests failing in staging on legacy payloads, working on adapters.
maria: test plan: 1) unit tests, 2) staging end-to-end with fuzzed payloads, 3) infra scan with runtime monitoring for suspicious process activity.
cheng: add Sysmon / auditd rule for java process spawning shells and outbound C2 patterns. I have a playbook snippet: ```auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -F pid=$(pgrep -f 'java.*inference-worker') -k java-exec```
liam: timeline: aim to patch inference-worker within 2 hours, model-ingest within 4 hours, telemetry-ingest within 8 hours. If blockers hit, escalate to oncall-SRE.
derek: patch in staging in 25m, running integration suite now.
anita: can we run a grep across current deployments for suspicious __type payloads? I'll query logs: `jq -r '.payload.__type' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head`
maria: good. also search for dynamic class load attempts in logs: `grep -E "URLClassLoader|defineClass" -R /var/log/services`
cheng: added detection rule to logging pipeline: emit alert if `__type` matches pattern `[a-zA-Z0-9_\.]+` and target service equals model-ingest.
devops-bot: alerting: new rule deployed to prod-logging at 1799997000
liam: once PRs merged — coordinate canary then global rollout. Keep rollback plan ready.
maria: communications & ticketing: created SEC-321 to track remediation. Add links to each PR in the ticket. Also file a customer-facing FAQ draft in SEC-321/docs.
anita: staged canary deployed for model-ingest, no errors after 15m. Rolling to blue-green in 10m.
derek: inference-worker passed canary tests, rolling prod now.
liam: SRE, please monitor for increased 500s or CPU spikes during rollout.
cheng: monitoring: added dashboard for unusual classloader errors and child process counts.
maria: after rollout, run dependency scan (SCA) org-wide and schedule automated PRs for minor bumps. We should also add jackson to our high-risk monitored list.
derek: postmortem TODOs: update onboarding docs to call out safe deserialization patterns, add lint rule to flag usage of `enableDefaultTyping`.
anita: telemetry-ingest upgrade queued, will deploy in 6 hours due to maintenance window.
liam: final: no signs of exploitation in our infra so far — good job rapid response team. We'll keep this thread open for any follow-ups and if anything shows up in IDS. :thumbsup:
